content.title: About
content.content: Crab salad is a ready‑to‑eat dish made from crab meat (or crab‑flavored surimi), mayonnaise, fresh vegetables, spices and sometimes a thickening agent. It has a delicate sea flavor, a light creamy texture and works well as an appetizer or light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crab salad is a common filling for sushi rolls, such as the California roll.
Traditional recipes use real crab meat, but mass‑produced versions often contain surimi imitation.
The salad is typically served chilled to highlight the freshness of the seafood.
Common add‑ins include corn, green onion, carrot, and hard‑boiled egg.
Crab salad is frequently included in ready‑made meal kits and party platters.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Crab meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many meat‑based salads, crab salad usually contains modest amounts of saturated fat.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Crab is rich in zinc, selenium and copper, which are important for immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Low cholesterol content and the presence of omega‑3 fatty acids help promote cardiovascular health.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to crab or its surimi substitute.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared salads often contain added salt, so people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Certain recipes use sweet sauces, increasing the calorie count.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Because it contains seafood, the salad spoils quickly; keep it refrigerated at +4 °C and consume within a few days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve crab salad chilled as a starter, in sandwiches, sushi rolls, or as a side to rice. Garnish with fresh herbs, lemon juice or capers to boost flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at +4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Discard if it develops an off odor or discoloration.
